sources_considered.why: Primary factual-writing evaluation; this version was available before the post.
Primary human evaluation directly challenges the summarization example.
Documents long-context weaknesses, but does not directly test full-book comprehension.

receipt.public_excerpt: InstructGPT and ChatGPT achieve FActScores of 42.5% and 58.3%, respectively.

evidence_items.explanation: Human checking found substantial unsupported factual content in generated biographies. This supports the factual-prose limitation for the tested systems and task, without establishing that all factual writing was beyond their competence.

receipt.public_excerpt: better factual consistency and fewer instances of extrinsic hallucinations

evidence_items.explanation: Across five summarization tasks, human evaluators preferred model summaries to the human references; the factuality comparison also favored GPT-4. This contradicts treating summarization generally as an activity contemporary systems could not perform competently.

The study documents weaknesses in multi-document question answering and retrieval from long inputs. It supplies relevant context but neither tests full-book comprehension nor establishes a human competence threshold.

unresolved_gaps: No directly comparable evaluation of hostile-witness cross-examination was established.
The cited long-context experiment does not settle full-book comprehension.
The factual-writing study lacks a matched human-writing baseline.
The evidence does not establish how many task categories meet a common competence threshold.
